cases.quote: Policies trained in one backend expect joints and links in a specific order determined by how that backend parses the robot model. When transferring to another backend, the joint ordering may be different, requiring remapping of observations and actions.
cases.symptom: Policy fed joint obs / emits actions in the wrong joint order when moved across backends.
cases.silent: yes (no error; a permuted vector is still a valid tensor)
cases.how_found: Official documentation; remap via YAML joint-name lists.
cases.root_cause: PhysX (BFS) and Newton/MJWarp parse the same USD into different joint/link orders.
cases.reproducibility: Direct: take a PhysX-trained Isaac-Velocity-Flat-Anymal-D or -G1 checkpoint, play it on newton_mjwarp without the YAML/ordering remap (permute action and joint_pos/joint_vel obs slices by the PhysX->MJWarp permutation). Serial chains (Franka) are identity and make a good negative control.
cases.quote_source: WebFetch summarizer extraction (verbatim not independently string-matched)

cases.quote: Setting only joint_ordering silently leaves bodies in backend order, which mismatches a checkpoint.
cases.symptom: Body-indexed quantities (contact sensors, body_ids in rewards/terminations, feet air-time) refer to the wrong bodies after a partial remap.
cases.how_found: Official docs for the Isaac Lab 3.x articulation ordering stack.
cases.root_cause: joint_ordering and body_ordering are independent knobs; root_view arrays stay in solver order regardless.
cases.reproducibility: Set joint_ordering='physx' but leave body_ordering=None on newton_mjwarp for ANYmal-D/G1 flat; any body-index-based term (undesired_contacts, feet_air_time, base_contact termination) now points at the wrong links. Also: index root_view arrays with find_joints() indices.
cases.quote_source: WebFetch summarizer extraction (verbatim not independently string-matched)

cases.quote: ANYmal-D transfer commands were missing their articulation ordering overrides.
cases.symptom: Official documented sim-to-sim transfer commands for the two branching robots omitted joint_ordering/body_ordering.
cases.how_found: Doc/PR review; validated PN and NP transfer on Isaac-Velocity-Rough-AnymalD and -G1 after fix.
cases.root_cause: G1 and ANYmal-D kinematic trees branch, so PhysX and MJWarp orders differ; Franka's serial chain is identical in both.
cases.reproducibility: Exactly the target setting: run documented transfer command for ANYmal-D/G1 with and without joint_ordering/body_ordering overrides; measure velocity-tracking error and fall rate.
cases.quote_source: gh CLI raw issue/PR text (quote string-matched verbatim)

cases.quote: a raw framework checkpoint (e.g. rsl_rl `.pt`) carries no record of the joint/body order the policy was trained against
cases.symptom: Replay depends on user remembering the training backend; convention resolution emulates backend traversal and a default change would silently yield a wrong permutation.
cases.silent: yes (design issue explicitly says 'silently produce a wrong permutation')
cases.root_cause: rsl_rl .pt stores weights only; ordering inferred symbolically at env creation.
cases.reproducibility: Train Go2/ANYmal-D flat on PhysX, then play with joint_ordering=None on newton_mjwarp (i.e. assume identity). Contrast with 'from_checkpoint' / explicit 'physx' convention.
cases.quote_source: gh CLI raw issue/PR text (quote string-matched verbatim)

cases.quote: The two arrays are in different spaces, so past the first ball joint they refer to different joints.
cases.symptom: Joint-position reads indexed wrong joints (knee obs read a quaternion w); reset writes corrupted pose (loop-closure residual 0.0004 mm -> 828 mm).
cases.how_found: Enabling Digit velocity tasks on Newton.
cases.root_cause: Newton joint_q is coordinate space (ball joint = 4 coords) vs joint_qd DOF space (3); MDP assumed 1:1.
cases.reproducibility: Not reproducible on GO2/G1/H1/ANYmal-D (all revolute: coord==DOF). Could only be emulated by an off-by-k index shift in joint_pos obs.
cases.quote_source: gh CLI raw issue/PR text (quote string-matched verbatim)

cases.quote: Joint effort targets are **silently not applied** by the PhysX backend on the isaacsim 6.0.1.0 stack: a constant effort command produces **zero** cart motion.
cases.symptom: Effort-controlled task untrainable on PhysX (reward plateau ~10) while Newton converges (~296/300); run looks normal.
cases.how_found: Cross-backend comparison of the same task/config.
cases.root_cause: set_dof_actuation_forces() effectively a no-op on that PhysX tensor-API stack; fixed by PR #7924.
cases.reproducibility: Relevant only for explicit/effort actuators. On GO2/ANYmal-D (ANYmal-D uses an explicit actuator-net/DC-motor model applying efforts) a controlled perturbation is to zero the applied effort on one backend; would show as training failure, not subtle bias.
cases.quote_source: gh CLI raw issue/PR text (quote string-matched verbatim)

cases.quote: Remove backend-specific task and training changes from rough velocity configurations so physics selection no longer silently changes the comparison inputs.
cases.symptom: Selecting a physics preset also changed armature and training budget, so PhysX vs Newton comparisons were confounded.
cases.root_cause: preset(default=..., newton_mjwarp=...) splits on non-physics task fields.
cases.reproducibility: Local checkout @2901490 still has go2/cassie rough_env_cfg armature=preset(default=0.0, newton_mjwarp=0.02): compare PhysX vs Newton with and without the split to measure how much of the backend gap is actually config.

cases.quote: Previously: PhysX used `armature=0.0`, Newton used a nonzero value (`0.02` for Go2/Go1/Cassie, `0.01` for Anymal C).
cases.symptom: Same task name ran with different actuator armature depending on backend; aligning raised PhysX reward (Go2 +6.6%, Go1 +19.2%, ANYmal-C +10.5%).
cases.how_found: OSMO sweep 4 robots x 2 arms x 3 seeds.
cases.root_cause: Backend-conditioned armature preset.
cases.reproducibility: Directly reproducible on Go2 flat/rough: armature 0.0 vs 0.02 on each backend (2x2), 3+ seeds.

cases.quote: Without it, velocity targets are silently ignored.
cases.symptom: ImplicitActuatorCfg gains written but target mode stays as imported from USD (EFFORT if USD drive gains zero), so PD targets inactive on Newton.
cases.root_cause: Newton infers joint_target_mode at USD import; MJWarp creates actuators at construction; later gain writes cannot add them.
cases.reproducibility: Use a USD with zero drive gains + ImplicitActuatorCfg stiffness on Go2 under newton_mjwarp vs PhysX. Would be loud (robot collapses) rather than subtle.

cases.quote: 3840 slots), so contacts were being dropped even in configurations where the guard does not fire.

cases.reproducibility: Flat Go2/G1 presets set nconmax=35/njmax=65 (local go2 flat_env_cfg). Perturbation: shrink nconmax/njmax below steady-state need on G1 flat and check overflow flags + gait metrics vs PhysX.

cases.root_cause: Fixed-size GPU buffers.

cases.reproducibility: Velocity tasks use history_length=3 so default is not affected; perturbation: set history_length=0 on Go2 contact sensor and compare undesired_contacts / base_contact termination rates PhysX vs Newton.

cases.quote: The sensor clock is a float32 accumulator whose rounding error reaches ~1e-6 after a few seconds of simulated time, roughly 100x the default tolerance, so the events vanished depending on the magnitude of the sim clock.
cases.symptom: compute_first_contact/air silently missed most touchdown/lift-off events after a few seconds.
cases.root_cause: abs_tol far below float32 timer error.
cases.reproducibility: Not backend-specific, but affects feet_air_time reward in GO2/ANYmal-D/G1 velocity tasks; a cross-backend study must pin the Isaac Lab version since pre/post-fix reward differs.
cases.quote_source: gh CLI raw issue/PR text (quote string-matched verbatim)
cases.note: Not a cross-backend divergence; included because it silently changes the reward used in the target tasks.
